classification.difficultyReason: Find three compatible pairs of negative fractions satisfying the sums on the sides of a triangular arrangement.

content.prompt: Place the numbers $-\frac{7}{5},\ -\frac{3}{2},\ -\frac{8}{5},\ -\frac{17}{10},\ -\frac{9}{5},\ -\frac{19}{10}$ in the circle so that the sum along any of the lines is $-\frac{57}{10}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Challenge exercise, question 5 triangular circle arrangement
spec.description: Nine white circles on the perimeter of an upright triangle, with two empty response circles between each pair of fixed vertex circles. Decorative blue outlines are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: Top vertex −11/10, bottom-left vertex −13/10, bottom-right vertex −6/5. Each straight side contains four circles and must sum to −57/10.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three supplied vertex values are visible.

answer.worked:
Write the supplied fractions in tenths. The two empty circles on each side must have the following sums:
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Left pair}&=-\frac{57}{10}+\frac{11}{10}+\frac{13}{10}\\
\text{Left pair}&=-\frac{33}{10}\\
\text{Right pair}&=-\frac{57}{10}+\frac{11}{10}+\frac{12}{10}\\
\text{Right pair}&=-\frac{34}{10}\\
\text{Bottom pair}&=-\frac{57}{10}+\frac{13}{10}+\frac{12}{10}\\
\text{Bottom pair}&=-\frac{32}{10}
\end{align*}$$
Choose the pairs $(-\frac75,-\frac{19}{10})$, $(-\frac95,-\frac85)$ and $(-\frac32,-\frac{17}{10})$, respectively. The completed arrangement gives:
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Left side}&=\frac{-11-14-19-13}{10}\\
\text{Left side}&=-\frac{57}{10}\\
\text{Right side}&=\frac{-11-18-16-12}{10}\\
\text{Right side}&=-\frac{57}{10}\\
\text{Bottom side}&=\frac{-13-15-17-12}{10}\\
\text{Bottom side}&=-\frac{57}{10}
\end{align*}$$
